newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, diffs stable, Bangchak awards.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, diffs stable, Bangchak awards.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Wednesday but differentials were mostly stable as Bangchak refinery soaked up some of the overhang in Murban crude.
The 120,000 bpd refinery purchased one million barrels at Dubai quotes around +$1.50/+$1.60 from Mitsubishi Corp.
A refinery source said it equated the Dubai-related level to ADNOC -20 cents.
The deal represents one of the first June Murban deals to emerge. Few other Murban deals have been seen by market players.
A U.S. major was said to have bought Murban as part of a package with Umm Shaif, but a price was not heard.
Bangchak also awarded a cargo of Oman at MPM -18 cents to Statoil, market sources said.
The refinery source said the refinery did not need to buy any regional light grades for June as the Murban purchases now provided enough light crude for the month.
That price was firmer than recent spot deals, which have been around MPM -20 cents per barrel and as low as MPM -22 cents.
Qatar Marine consolidated its price level around QGPC -45 cents as a U.S. major sold a cargo to a Japanese trader, reflecting a deal at a similar level on Monday.
Lower Zakum, which had also only been lightly traded until now, was traded twice to a U.S. major at ADNOC -10 cents by two Japanese traders.
Traders said buyers were now emerging ahead of the release of official selling prices of Middle East grades this week.
The OSPs are widely expected to fall, which will offer some upward relief to market differentials.
The rush by late buyers was likely to mean that the worse of the weakness of the Middle East grades was over, traders said.
